raw_text: DURING REMOVING PIN FROM A STRUCTURE, ONE RIGMAN HAMMERED THE PIN TO REMOVE IT AND IT CAME OUT AT SPEED PASSING NEARBY TO THE RIGMAN HOLDING THE PIN STANDING OPPOSITE TO IT.
root_cause_analysis: UNAWARENESS OF RIGMAN STANDING EXACT OPPOSITE TO DIRECTION OF BLOW.
potential_consequences: IT COULD HAVE HIT ANYWHERE RESULTING TO MINOR TO MAJOR INJURY.
corrective_action: INSTRUCTED ALL CREW MEMBERS TO WORK SAFELY.
preventive_action: 1. DON'T HOLD PIN WHEN HAMMERING. 2. IF REQUIRED TO HOLD, THEN STAND AND HOLD AWAY FROM THE POSSIBLE OUT DIRECTION OF BLOW.

raw_text: DURING LINE TESTING, ONE PERSON WAS TIGHTENING THE JOINT WITH HAMMER. SUDDENLY THE HAMMER GOT SLIPPED FROM HIS HAND AND FELL DOWN ON THE GROUND. LUCKILY NO ONE GOT INJURED.
root_cause_analysis: DUE TO THE CARELESSNESS OF THE PERSON.
potential_consequences: IT MAY HIT PERSONS STANDING NEARBY AND CAUSE SERIOUS INJURY.
corrective_action: INSTRUCTED ALL CREW MEMBERS TO WORK SAFELY WITH WEARING FULL PPE.
preventive_action: ENSURE MANUAL IMPACT TOOLS ARE TETHERED AND DROP ZONE BARRICADED.

raw_text: DURING ROUTINE CHECKUP, IT WAS OBSERVED THAT EYEWASH FITTED AT THE DERRICK FLOOR WAS PROPERLY FILLED WITH WATER.
potential_consequences: DELAYED EYE FLUSHING DURING CHEMICAL OR MUD SPLASH.
corrective_action: IMMEDIATELY CLEAN THE EYEWASH AND FILLED WITH WATER PROPERLY.
preventive_action: ALWAYS KEEP THE EYEWASH FILLED WITH CLEANED WATER AT DERRICK FLOOR AND AT CHEMICAL STORES.

raw_text: During morning shift, Valve A on the Rig-04 manifold was opened to bleed surface pressure as per workover schedule. Pressure gauge dropped from 210 bar to near-zero over approximately 15 minutes. Operation was completed without incident. Crew proceeded to change the manifold spool piece following the bleed-down.

Welding crew commenced cutting operations on the old gas injection flowline near the production manifold on Well-Pad B. Work started at approximately 10:00 hrs. Grinder was used to prepare flanges for welding. The weather was dry and wind was from the southwest.

Pedestal crane was observed lifting a 2.5 tonne BOP component from the laydown area to the rig floor. During the lift, two workers were seen walking beneath the crane boom near the suspended load. Lift supervisor radioed crane operator and the load was lowered immediately after the observation.

Two technicians entered the sour gas production area at Rig-07 to investigate a reported high-pressure reading on the wellhead pressure transmitter. The area is designated H2S Zone 2. Technicians were wearing standard coveralls and hard hats. Investigation took approximately 20 minutes.

Maintenance team removed the flanged connection on the high-pressure gas injection line (rated 420 bar) to replace a corroded gasket. Bolts were progressively removed and the flange was backed off. Work was proceeding in the morning shift. Three technicians were involved in the flanging-out operation.

A worker was found inside Storage Tank T-04 at the tank farm, conducting an internal inspection for corrosion mapping. Worker had entered through the top manhole approximately 45 minutes earlier. One supervisor was present at the site office, approximately 30 meters from the tank.

Electrician was observed performing maintenance on the 11kV switchboard in MCC Room-3. The switchboard houses the main distribution for the process area. Electrician had removed the panel cover and was working on the bus-bar terminations. Site electrical supervisor confirmed the work order was in the system.

Worker was transferring concentrated hydrochloric acid (HCl, 35%) from a 200-litre drum into smaller dispensing containers for use in scale removal on the wellhead. Worker was wearing a standard site uniform. The transfer operation was carried out using a manual pump.

Technicians commenced disassembly of the high-pressure injection pump (P-102) at Wellhead Pad-5 early morning. Pump was removed from the skid and bolts were being undone on the pump body. Work had been ongoing for approximately 2 hours when the area HSE officer arrived for his morning round.

Two workers observed performing maintenance on heat exchanger E-201 at the process plant. The heat exchanger is mounted at approximately 6.5 meters elevation on a pipe rack. Workers had accessed the unit via a temporary scaffold installed yesterday. Both workers were seen kneeling on the scaffold top rail.

Diesel bowser (10,000 litre capacity) arrived to refuel the rig generators. The driver reversed the bowser to the fuel point and connected the delivery hose to the generator day tank. Delivery of approximately 5,000 litres commenced. Operation was completed in 25 minutes without spill.

Night shift operators bypassed the high-pressure ESD on Compressor Unit-3 to allow maintenance work on the recycle valve actuator. The ESD was taken out of service at 02:15 hrs. Actuator replacement was completed by 05:45 hrs. ESD was reinstated before day shift takeover.

Worker reported near-slip on the main access walkway near the mud logging unit on Rig-03. The walkway had accumulated drilling fluid residue from activities earlier in the shift. Worker caught themselves on the handrail. No injury resulted. Area was cleaned with absorbent material and mopped dry.

Operator noticed unusual gas odour near the wellhead of Well-12 during routine morning checks. H2S personal detector did not alarm but hydrocarbon odour was distinct. Work in the area was suspended and production supervisor notified. Area gas test was requested. Gas test showed 8% LEL at ground level near the flowline connection. Leaking instrument valve was found and isolated.

Fire extinguisher at Station 7 on the drill floor was found expired during monthly inspection. Extinguisher label showed last test date of 14 months ago (annual test required). Extinguisher was tagged out of service and replacement requested from stores. Area was covered by adjacent extinguisher (Station 6) in the interim.

Excavation work for cable trench was observed with inadequate barricading on the access road side. The trench was approximately 1.8 metres deep and 0.6 metres wide. One side had no barrier, with a gap of approximately 3 metres. A temporary warning cone had fallen over. Foreman was instructed to immediately re-barricade the trench.

Forklift operator was observed traveling at approximately 18–20 km/h in the warehouse area. Site speed limit is 10 km/h. Operator was carrying a pallet of drilling chemicals. No incident occurred. Operator was stopped and reminded of the speed limit and warned of consequences for further violations.

During tubing retrieval operations at Well-08, NORM-contaminated tubing was pulled and laid out on the pipe rack without NORM survey being conducted first. Radiation survey was eventually performed 2 hours later, confirming scale contamination on 14 joints. Appropriate NORM barriers were then established and personnel were notified.

Pressure test on the new gas injection spool at Test Manifold-2 was conducted with only one technician present. The test reached 350 bar (1.25x operating pressure per API standard). The two-person attendance rule for high-pressure testing above 200 bar was not observed. No failure occurred during the test.

Scale inhibitor spillage (approximately 30 litres) occurred at the chemical injection skid when a pump seal failed. Spill was contained within the bunded area. Clean-up commenced 4 hours after the spill due to availability of hazmat clean-up materials. Pump was isolated and tagged. MSDS classification: irritant, non-flammable.

Worker reported onset of lower back pain after manually lifting 14 lengths of 2-inch tubing from ground level to a transportation frame. Individual lengths weighed approximately 22 kg each. No mechanical lifting aid was used. Worker was taken to medical and assessed — soft tissue strain confirmed. Returned to light duties.

Emergency muster drill conducted at 09:00 hrs. Muster point accountability took 14 minutes total. Three personnel were initially unaccounted for — two were on a water flush operation at the far wellhead and one had not heard the alarm. All three were located within 8 minutes. Drill findings to be incorporated into emergency response procedure review.

Routine external inspection of gas injection pipeline GI-07 found severe external corrosion on two flanged joints in the buried section. Corrosion depth estimated at 35–40% of wall thickness. Area marked and operations supervisor notified. Cathodic protection survey ordered. Pipeline continued in service pending integrity assessment.

Night shift inspection found portable lighting in the separator maintenance area to be inadequate. Two of five temporary work lights had failed bulbs and were unlit. Technicians were working on separator instrumentation under the remaining three lights. Natural lighting from the adjacent floodlights was insufficient to cover the full work area.

Monthly inspection of emergency response equipment found three SCBA sets with expired hydrostatic test dates on the cylinder. Testing is required every 5 years per manufacturer specification and OISD-RP-187. The expired units were tagged out of service and sent for testing. Working units were redistributed.

Permit was issued for maintenance on compressor suction filter at Compressor Building-2. Technicians had proceeded to start work on removal of the filter housing before the Job Safety Analysis (JSA) for the task was completed and signed. PTW had been issued but the JSA section was blank. Work was stopped and JSA completed before resuming.

Safety shower at the acid injection skid was found to be blocked by three 200-litre chemical drums stored temporarily against the shower unit. The shower was completely inaccessible. Area safety officer ordered immediate removal of the drums. Shower was tested and found operational once cleared.

H2S gas alarm activated in the production control room at 14:22 hrs indicating H2S detection at the Rig-04 wellhead area. Muster was initiated. Investigation found that the alarm was caused by a malfunctioning sensor (condensation ingress). No actual H2S release confirmed. Sensor was replaced. Muster completed and personnel stood down after 35 minutes.

Worker observed not wearing a hard hat while walking through the PPE-mandatory zone near the site office compound. Worker was carrying a stack of documents and had removed their hard hat to wipe their forehead. Worker was reminded of PPE requirements and immediately replaced their hard hat.

Oily rags and used cleaning cloths found stored in an open cardboard box approximately 1.5 metres from the generator exhaust stack on Rig-06. Combustion risk from proximity to heat source. Rags were immediately placed into approved metal waste container and removed from the area.

Safety and emergency information signs at the main site entrance are severely faded and not legible from vehicle distance. Signs include emergency assembly point directions, site speed limit, and PPE requirements. Photographed for maintenance request. Temporary laminated signs to be placed pending sign replacement.

First aid kit in the driller's cabin on Rig-01 found with depleted contents. Missing items include: 10 bandages (various sizes), 3 sterile gauze pads, antiseptic wipes, and two cold packs. Kit label shows last inspection 6 weeks ago. Stores requested to replenish. Supplementary first aid kit identified in tool pusher office as interim cover.

Operator observed wearing open-toed sandals while inspecting wellhead equipment in an area requiring safety footwear. When approached, operator stated their safety boots were wet from an earlier spill and they were allowing them to dry. Operator was instructed to return to accommodation to change and not re-enter the work area without proper footwear.

Standing water observed on the floor near the main control room entrance following overnight heavy rain. Water was pooling at the bottom step creating a slip hazard. Caution cones placed immediately. Drainage was cleared and floor dried within 30 minutes. Permanent drainage solution to be reviewed.

Day shift commenced at 06:00 hrs on Rig-02 without a documented pre-shift safety meeting (toolbox talk). Shift supervisor stated the meeting was conducted verbally during walk-around but no attendance record was completed. Corrective action: toolbox talk register to be completed and signed by all shift personnel within 30 minutes of shift start.

Vehicle driver observed using a mobile phone (holding it to their ear) while driving on the main site road. Driver was a third-party logistics contractor. Vehicle was stopped and driver warned. Incident reported to contractor site representative. Company safe driving policy does not permit use of handheld devices while driving on site.

Floor of the mud room found slippery due to drilling fluid residue. Non-slip matting had been removed for cleaning 3 days ago and not yet replaced. Two workers had nearly slipped during the shift but caught themselves. Temporary warning cones placed. Non-slip mats ordered from stores.

Safety harness found hanging unsecured on an open hook in the equipment store without a proper storage bag or rack. Visual inspection showed the harness had signs of UV degradation on the webbing. Harness was tagged out of service pending formal inspection by the rigging inspector. Two new harnesses confirmed in stock as replacements.

Fire escape route on the ground floor of Office Building B found partially obstructed by three office chairs and a filing cabinet that had been temporarily moved during office rearrangement. Obstruction narrowed the escape corridor to less than 50% of its required width. Items were immediately moved and clear passage restored.

Worker reported observing another worker smoking in the non-designated area near the camp accommodation block. The smoking area is clearly marked 50 metres from the accommodation. Reported worker was spoken to by the camp supervisor and reminded of the policy. Incident logged for records.

Monthly PPE inspection found three pairs of safety boots with cracked or compromised toe caps. Workers wearing the affected boots were identified and issued with new footwear from stores. Damaged boots were collected and disposed of to prevent reuse. Monthly inspection record updated.

A site visitor (contractor inspector) was observed walking unescorted in the process area. The visitor had signed in at the main gate but the escort assignment had not been completed when the visitor proceeded on-site. Visitor was intercepted and escorted back to the reception area. Visitor policy reviewed with gate security.

Workshop tool storage area found disorganized with various hand tools (spanners, hammers, socket sets) stored loosely on wall-mounted pegboards without any securing mechanism. Tools could fall if the pegboard is vibrated. Dropped tool risk in the area below. Workshop supervisor to organize tool storage with retaining clips or labeled drawers.

SDS (Safety Data Sheet) binder in the chemical storage room found to be missing the sheet for the newly arrived biocide product (Glutaraldehyde 50%). Chemical has been in storage for 2 weeks. SDS was obtained from the supplier and added to the binder. Chemical storage register updated.

Fluorescent tube lights in the main parts storeroom have been malfunctioning for the past week. Three of eight tubes are either flickering or not illuminating. Storeroom personnel have been using mobile phone torches to locate parts in dim areas. Maintenance work order raised for lighting replacement.

Company vehicle (site pickup truck) observed ignoring the 15 km/h speed limit on Site Road B near the wellpad entrance. Speed was estimated at approximately 30 km/h. Vehicle was not stopped (driver not identified). CCTV footage requested to identify driver. Speed bump installation to be expedited at this location.

Site canteen ventilation fan found inoperable at lunchtime. With approximately 40 workers dining at peak time, CO2 level from breathing may accumulate and the cooking fumes from the kitchen area were noticeable throughout the dining area. Fan motor replacement ordered. Temporary measure: door propped open for cross-ventilation.

Safety bulletin board near the main operations building found with multiple outdated notices. The most recent site emergency contact list displayed was from 2022. A seasonal heat stress advisory was still posted from last year. Board was cleaned and updated with current emergency contacts, IOGP reminders, and current month safety theme material.

During daily vehicle inspection, a site pickup truck was found with a large crack running across the passenger side of the windshield, approximately 40 cm in length. Vehicle was grounded pending windshield replacement. Driver had been using the vehicle for 3 days with the cracked windshield without reporting it. Driver counseled.

New contract worker observed operating in the Rig-01 work area without a site induction record visible on the HRIS system. Worker had been on site for 2 days. Upon investigation, site induction had been conducted but the record had not been entered into the system by the HSE department. Record was located in paper form and digitized. System access now confirmed.
